story: Ilmarinen is an immortal artificer god who works brass, copper, iron, gold, and silver. He forged the dome of the sky and once forged an iron rake for a swallow so it could gather pieces of its broken eggs, which became the sun, moon, and clouds. Elsewhere, an island at the center of the world was born when a drop of boiling gold fell from his pot into the sea. He also struck the first spark of fire using three eagle feathers, and forged the first iron, which swore never to hurt anyone but broke its promise after a hornet brought snake poison into its quenching water. In one tale, Ilmarinen forged a sword and a stallion, then worked the bellows himself and created a maiden of gold, but she was cold to lie beside, teaching that men should never make a maiden of gold and silver. In the great tale of the Sampo, the sage Väinämöinen was held captive by Louhi, mistress of Pohjola, who demanded a magic Sampo be forged in exchange for safe passage and her daughter's hand. Väinämöinen tricked Ilmarinen into traveling to Pohjola. There, seeing the maiden's beauty, Ilmarinen agreed to forge the Sampo. Over days he cast a crossbow, a ship, a cow, and a plow from his forge, each one flawed and destroyed. Finally, after conjuring four winds, the Sampo emerged as a mill producing grain, salt, and gold. Louhi locked it away, and though Ilmarinen asked the maiden to marry him, she refused, and he returned home alone. Later, after losing his wife to a curse, he forged a new wife of gold, but she was cold; his brother refused to marry her and told him to melt her down into trinkets instead.
